body: Any chance you can attach a small project that reproduces the behavior you mention?

I have updated the reproduce to make it more focused.

[quarkus-main-db-problem.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22009177/quarkus-main-db-problem.zip)

The problem with this is that when the test method of the `@QuarkusMainTest` is executed, it is using the System ClassLoader instead of the Quarkus Runtime ClassLoader.

@holly-cummins any idea why this is happening?

> The problem with this is that when the test method of the `@QuarkusMainTest` is executed, it is using the System ClassLoader instead of the Quarkus Runtime ClassLoader.
> 
> [@holly-cummins](https://github.com/holly-cummins) any idea why this is happening?

So I'm pretty sure this is by design. Certainly, for this particular reproducer, the problem is present as far back as I culd be bothered to check (Quarkus 3.9). `@QuarkusMainTest` has never done the same classloader dance as `@QuarkusTest`, to ensure test methods are run with the application classloader. 

I've just checked the [docs](https://quarkus.io/guides/command-mode-reference#mocking), and they confirm CDI injection isn't supported in `QuarkusMainTest`, so by (liberal) extension, access to modified entities also isn't expected to work. I can think of a few possible workarounds: 
- Just use `@QuarkusTest` for tests which want to poke at the database. Adding a `@TestProfile` and setting `runMainMethod` might help with your use case.
- Add some special test-mode diagnostic arguments to the app and then read the output from `LaunchResult`. It's a bit ugly, though. 
- Use old-school APIs to access the database.

> I've just checked the [docs](https://quarkus.io/guides/command-mode-reference#mocking), and they confirm CDI injection isn't supported in QuarkusMainTest, so by (liberal) extension, access to modified entities also isn't expected to work

That pretty much settles it then :)

We should probably also update the docs to mention that Panache doesn't work there either

> We should probably also update the docs to mention that Panache doesn't work there either

Yeah, I think the expected pattern would be to use `@QuarkusMainTest` just to exercise your launch arguments and sense check that the command basically does the thing and produces reasonable output, and `@QuarkusTest` for digging into the functionality. 

In other words, `@QuarkusTest` should be the main test mechanism and `@QuarkusMainTest` would be the less important secondary test mechanism. With hindsight, `@QuarkusCommandTest` might have been a better name for the thing that isn't main 😂
